images.title: Adding 4s against multiplying 4s
images.purpose: Contrasts 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 with 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 so that repeated multiplication is seen to grow much faster.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A before and after comparison: two panels side by side, separated by a thin grey vertical line.
images.exact_structure: Left panel: three groups of 4 amber (#E69F00) dots in a row, 12 dots in all, with the label adding above and 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 below. Right panel: one cube built from small teal (#0072B2) unit cubes, 4 along each edge, drawn in simple flat isometric view so that each of the three visible faces shows a 4 by 4 grid of 16 squares, 64 unit cubes in all; the label multiplying above and 4 × 4 × 4 = 4³ = 64 below. A thin grey (#6B7280) vertical divider between the panels. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Repeated addition of 4 gives 12, but repeated multiplication of 4 gives 64.
images.description: Contrasts 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 with 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 so that repeated multiplication is seen to grow much faster.

image_decisions.why: Seeing 12 dots beside a 64 cube shows why a power is not the base times the exponent.
